document.abstract: The production industry is experiencing mounting pressure to deliver more content on more platforms, leading producers to deliver on-demand and over-the-top (OTT) media using software- and cloud-based solutions. The growth in both volume of content and the use of Internet Protocol (IP)-based delivery methods comes at an environmental cost, in terms of energy consumption and physical waste. The hyperconverged design approach combines production capabilities into a single product and offers engineers and designers immediate ways to reduce a production’s environmental impact while simultaneously simplifying its deployment, management, and operation. Throughout the product lifecycle, from design to disposition, hyperconverged products can support the media and entertainment industry in achieving sustainability targets, which protect and conserve the environment.

authors.bio: Alun Fryer is the technical marketing lead for Hyperconverged Solutions at Ross Video, Ottawa, ON, Canada. He serves as a marketing liaison to research and development (the voice of the customer), a technical liaison between product marketing and end users (making the technology make sense), and engages in Ross’ global thought-leadership program. He has previously held several roles in product development bringing many well-known products from concept to reality, including the Synergy and Vision production switcher series. He has been actively involved with many trade organizations, including SMPTE, Advanced Media Workflow Association (AMWA), Joint Taskforce for Networked Media (JT-NM), and Alliance for IP Media Solutions (AIMS) where he served as the inaugural chair of the Education Working Group.
authors.name: Alun Fryer

authors.bio: Amanda Holtstrom is the product manager for DashBoard and Ross Platform Manager at Ross Video, Ottawa, ON, Canada. A computer engineer, she has spent her career designing and delivering software systems to address key problems in a variety of industries. An advocate for great design and simple interfaces, she joined Ross Video more than three years ago and is responsible for delivering core technologies to unite the Ross Video product portfolio.
